text:
Midway through the third, the Oilers had this one. They led 4-1. Then, in just over five minutes, St. Louis scored three times, and Edmonton left Enterprise Center with one point and a long flight home.

For two periods it was Edmonton's game. Kasperi Kapanen tipped one in at 5:56 of the first, with Connor Murphy and Connor McDavid assisting. Leon Draisaitl made it 2-0 in the second, his 1,100th career point. Dalibor Dvorsky answered at 17:44, but Filip Hallander restored the two-goal lead 45 seconds later, his first goal and first point as an Oiler on a night he was expected to skate on McDavid's line. Colton Dach made it 4-1 at 4:40 of the third.

Then it turned. Philip Broberg, the defenseman Edmonton drafted eighth overall in 2019, fired a slap shot through at 10:27, a 3% chance and the least likely goal of the game. He played 29:42. Pavel Buchnevich batted one in at 15:12, and 26 seconds later Jimmy Snuggerud deflected one in, from Justin Barron and Robert Thomas, to tie it. That goal alone moved St. Louis from 12% to 52%, and Snuggerud led everyone with 0.40 wins added. Tristan Jarry did make the save of the night, stopping Logan Mailloux on an 80% chance in the third, but he allowed 1.35 goals more than his 27 shots deserved.

Overtime settled nothing. In the shootout, McDavid scored and Jake Neighbours answered, Draisaitl was stopped, Mason McTavish scored, and Joel Hofer stopped Owen Michaels to end it.

The Blues have now won four straight, and this is the kind of win that makes a streak feel real. The Oilers will feel they lost it more than the Blues won it: 66 shot attempts to 48, 3.39 expected goals to 2.65, and our replays of every shot had Edmonton winning 63% of the time. Daily Faceoff Edmonton called it a "frustrating shootout loss" to end the road trip, which sounds about right.
headline: Blues erase three-goal hole, beat Oilers in shootout
